articles.title: Giants without Deonte Banks; Puka Nacua won’t play Monday for Rams
articles.summary: Giants will be short-handed at cornerback; Aaron Donald will play for Rams.
articles.body:
The New York Giants will be without starting cornerback Deonte Banks in Monday night's matchup with the Los Angeles Rams . Star wide receiver Puka Nacua won't play for the Rams.

Banks has a calf injury. He was listed as questionable, but did not practice Friday or Saturday. Nakua was an All-Pro last season, catching 129 passes.

The Giants also put cornerback Paulson Adebo on injured reserve last week. Linebacker Micah McFadden (neck) is also inactive.

Second-year defensive tackle Darius Alexander is also inactive. The Giants added veteran nose tackle Josh Tupou to the 53-man roster last week.

Star defensive tackle Aaron Donald is active for what will be his first NFL game since retiring at the end of the 2023 season.

articles.title: Nuggets rumors: The honest truth about Nikola Jokic's future in Denver
articles.summary: While one NBA analyst is questioning All-Star Nikola Jokic’s future with the Denver Nuggets, another believes it’s secure regardless of how the 2026-27 seaso...
articles.body:
While one NBA analyst is questioning All-Star Nikola Jokic 's future with the Denver Nuggets , another believes it's secure regardless of how the 2026-27 season develops. Jokic is expected to sign a historic extension with the Nuggets in 2027, which is why it's hard to fathom him signing elsewhere.

Jokic will be eligible for a whopping five-year, $359.5 million extension next summer , which should keep him with the Nuggets, as ESPN's Brian Windhorst noted, per The Hoop Collective podcast.

"Eastern European players, they don't have a history of plotting to exit in free agency," Windhorst said. "Those players typically like the teams that they grow up with. Even Giannis , Giannis is Greek. I think if all things are equal, Giannis wanted to stay in Milwaukee . And part of the reason why it was so messy to get Giannis was that he didn't necessarily want to do it. I don't think Jokic wants to leave. His circle is outrageously small.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"At the same time, he knows all this. He understands. He's one of the smartest guys in the league. So, on one hand, if you're looking at this future Power Rankings and you're saying, boy, this is a tough spot, and you're looking at Jokic saying, is he really going to go into the back of his prime in this situation, we should plot to try to get him. At the same time, it just seems totally out of his character and personality to plot to get out of the situation."

Nikola Jokic and the Nuggets, who finished 18th on ESPN's Future Power Rankings, will have their work cut out for themselves amidst a competitive Western Conference, led by the defending champion San Antonio Spurs and the 2024 Finals champion Oklahoma City Thunder . Still, inking arguably the best player in the NBA to a long-term extension doesn't guarantee Denver will be a top team in the league, as ESPN's Dave McMenamin pessimistically noted.

"I take him at his word that it is purely a business decision, financially, to wait to sign his contract," McMenamin said. "However, in doing that, that still puts the Nuggets — you give him the contract, you don't let the best player in franchise history, one of the best players of this generation, go, if you can keep him — but their ability to build anything close to a contender with Jokic making the most money in the league, the highest salary in the league, it's going to be hard. Really hard.

"Especially with all their picks out the door. I don't see the Nuggets being a legitimate contender for the rest of Jokic's career."

The Nuggets, who lost Tim Hardaway Jr. and Peyton Watson via free agency this summer, will have to fill the void left in their respective absences at the wing position, as McMenamin pointed out.

"They lost their two best bench players in Hardaway, and Peyton Watson was a part-time starter, but they lost two key rotation players," McMenamin said. "With the money, Jokic has stated reasons for waiting and not signing the extension this summer. He wants to maximize the contract. It's literally the biggest contract in the history of the league."

With the option to sign a four-year, $278 million extension over the summer, Nikola Jokic choosing the more lucrative offer in 2027 isn't out of the norm for a three-time MVP looking to maximize his dollars four years removed from leading the Nuggets to a championship in 2023.

With Denver's finances set up for the foreseeable future, the Nuggets have their core players, such as Jamal Murray and Aaron Gordon , locked in alongside Jokic, ESPN's Bobby Marks added.

"Well, they're the only team in the second apron. Jokic, of course, has a player option for next year," Marks said. "They're locked into that Aaron Gordon contract. Christian Braun is on that rookie extension, which is a big number. Cam Johnson could be a free agent, and Jamal Murray is on a max. You're basically top-heavy, and I think that shows you where your bench is. You're basically going to spend the minimum wheel every offseason."

Jokic, who finished second in MVP voting to Thunder's Shai Gilgeous-Alexander for the second season in a row, averaged 27.7 points on 56.9% shooting, including 38% from deep, also posted career-bests in rebounds (12.9), and assists (10.7) per game in 2025-26.

articles.title: Eagles bringing back fan favorite tight end Zach Ertz, AP sources say
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are bringing back fan favorite tight end Zach Ertz, three people familiar with the situation told The Associated Press.  Ertz will jo...
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles are bringing back fan favorite tight end Zach Ertz , three people familiar with the situation told The Associated Press.

Ertz will join the practice squad in hopes of shoring up a tight end room depleted by injuries, the people said Monday on condition of anonymity because the move had not been announced.

Ertz's return comes with multiple Eagles tight ends dealing with injuries.

Dallas Goedert is expected to miss several weeks with an MCL sprain suffered in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Tennessee Titans , one person told the AP. Backups Eli Stowers and Grant Calcaterra also are injured.

Ertz spent his first eight seasons with the Eagles, earning three Pro Bowl appearances, and made two key plays late in their Super Bowl win after the 2018 season. He played three seasons for Arizona after being traded in 2021 and spent the last two in Washington.

The 35-year-old suffered a torn ACL with the Commanders in December, but has been cleared to play.

Ertz is fifth on the NFL's career list for catches by a tight end with 825 and his 8,952 yards receiving are eighth. He's scored 57 touchdowns.

articles.title: Dodgers activate two key players immediately before big Padres series
articles.summary: The Dodgers can clinch a first-round postseason bye at home against the Padres
articles.body:
With one week left in the MLB regular season, the Los Angeles Dodgers are getting two key players back for a three-game home series against the San Diego Padres .

Pitcher Roki Sasaki and center fielder Andy Pages , who have been on the injured list since August, were activated from the injured list on Monday, an off-day for the Dodgers and Padres. The two National League West rivals can each clinch something important at Dodger Stadium — San Diego , a berth in the postseason, Los Angeles , a first-round bye.

Sasaki had a 3.05 ERA in seven starts post-All-Star-break when he developed a blister on his throwing hand in August. Pages played in his first All-Star Game in July, then fractured a bone in his right hand on Aug. 21, when he was hit by a 100.2 mph fastball from Pittsburgh Pirates starter Bubba Chandler .

The Dodgers managed to clinch the National League West without the two players, but both figure to play key roles in October for the defending World Series champions.

The Dodgers lost hard-throwing reliever Edgardo Henriquez to a back injury earlier this month . For all his second-half success as a starter, the Dodgers need Sasaki more in their bullpen as a right-handed compliment to left-handers Tanner Scott and Alex Vesia .

Pages, meanwhile, was excelling at the plate and in the field prior to his injury, which required surgery. He'll have six games to tune up for the postseason — and a chance at redemption for last October.

The Dodgers won the World Series even though Pages had only four hits in 16 postseason games, collecting an .078 batting average across four playoff rounds.

Without Pages, the Dodgers moved veteran utilityman Tommy Edman to center field. Through week's end, he was slashing .245/.328/.376 (94 OPS+) in 79 games this season.

The Dodgers are also expecting Shohei Ohtani to return during the Padres series, but he isn't eligible to be activated from the 15-day injured list before Wednesday.

In correpsonding 26-man roster moves, pitcher Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliezer Alfonzo were optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City.

articles.title: Robert Wolk Spent 30 Years Racing at the Limit. Parking Lot Road Rage Killed Him.
articles.summary: Robert Wolk built a three-decade career out of deliberately running out of grip in controlled conditions, and he survived all of it. On Wednesday, 16 Septemb...
articles.body:
Robert Wolk built a three-decade career out of deliberately running out of grip in controlled conditions, and he survived all of it. On Wednesday, 16 September, he was killed on a suburban corner in Kempton Park at something close to walking pace, after a bump minor enough that he got out of his Audi to look at the damage. He was 41, he was on his way to the airport, and he had a race entry waiting for him in Cape Town.

Motorsport South Africa confirmed the death and described a career that ran from junior karting in the mid-1990s to a national touring car title in 2024. Sport, Arts and Culture Minister Gayton McKenzie, in a government statement issued on Saturday, called the killing "an act of senseless violence, on our roads." Three men were in custody by the end of that week.

What police say happened on Camwood Street

Gauteng police place the shooting at the corner of Camwood Street and Portland Drive in Esther Park, a quiet residential pocket of Kempton Park a short drive from OR Tambo International. According to police spokesperson Colonel Dimakatso Nevhuhulwi, Wolk's Audi was involved in a minor collision. He got out to assess and photograph the damage, an argument followed, a firearm was produced, and he was declared dead at the scene. A murder docket was opened, and the sequence was captured on CCTV, footage that has since been passed around social media by people who should know better. We are not linking it.

There is a bitter detail buried in that account. Photographing damage at the scene is exactly what every insurer, every broker and every fleet policy tells you to do. Wolk was following the script.

Three accused, and why a first appearance matters more than it looks

Police made one arrest on Thursday, 18 September, and two more on Friday, 19 September. The three men are aged between 24 and 33. A firearm and a vehicle were seized for forensic and ballistic work, and all three were due before the Kempton Park Magistrates' Court on Monday, 21 September, on a charge of murder.

A first appearance in South Africa is mostly procedural: charges are put, legal representation is sorted, and the matter is usually postponed for further investigation. The real fight is bail, and South African bail law is structured in a way most people outside the system do not appreciate. Murder is a Schedule 5 offence under the Criminal Procedure Act, which inverts the ordinary presumption and puts the burden on the accused to show that release serves the interests of justice. If the State alleges the killing was planned or premeditated, or that the accused acted in furtherance of a common purpose, the matter climbs to Schedule 6, where the accused must prove exceptional circumstances. With three men charged over one shooting, common purpose is on the table from day one.

Sentencing follows the same fork. Under the minimum sentencing regime introduced by the Criminal Law Amendment Act of 1997, murder that is premeditated or committed in execution of a common purpose carries life imprisonment as the prescribed starting point. Murder outside that bracket carries a 15-year minimum for a first offender, unless a court finds substantial and compelling reasons to go lower. Which is why the seized pistol matters so much: ballistics linking a specific weapon to the fatal round is usually what converts a group arrest into individual liability.

Wolk's record reads like three different drivers' careers stapled together. He took South African Junior GP karting titles in 1995 and 1997, collected multiple Formula Ford championships, won the SA Formula Volkswagen crown in 2013 and the SA Formula 1600 title in 2015, then went back-to-back in SA GTC in 2021 and 2022 before adding the SA Touring Cars championship in 2024. He received Junior Protea Colours in 1998 and Senior Protea Colours in 2022.

That spread is far harder than a list of trophies makes it look. Formula Ford and Formula 1600 are momentum cars: skinny tyres, almost no downforce, and a driving style built on refusing to scrub speed. Braking is a suggestion. GTC machinery is the opposite animal, a tube-frame silhouette racer wearing a showroom shell over a purpose-built chassis, with real aero load, real slick grip and a braking technique that punishes anyone still driving like a single-seater hero. Plenty of quick drivers cross that divide and look ordinary for a full season while they recalibrate. Wolk kept winning through the switch, in a national structure where testing budgets are thin and there is no simulator programme waiting to bail you out.

This was not a veteran winding down. In May he won his second King of the Hill title at the Simola Hillclimb in Knysna, an event run on roughly two kilometres of closed public road where the scenery consists of stone, banks and trees, one car goes at a time, and the margin for a misjudged entry is measured in centimetres. In June he came back to SA Touring Cars and won at Aldo Scribante outside Gqeberha. He was entered at Killarney International Raceway in Cape Town for the weekend of his death.

Circuit racing has spent a century engineering its way out of killing people, with barrier research, halo devices, fire suppression, extraction crews and medical response times that most public health systems would envy. It is not perfect, as the rescue of Ollie Millroy from a burning Ferrari in Shanghai made uncomfortably clear. But it is a system, and it improves every decade. None of it applies on a residential corner on a Wednesday morning.

The part every driver should actually take from this

South Africa's National Road Traffic Act sets out what you owe after a crash: stop, check for injuries and damage, give your name, address and vehicle particulars to anyone with a reasonable interest, and report the incident at a police station within 24 hours if those details were not exchanged. Nothing in that obliges you to conduct a roadside negotiation with a stranger, and nothing in it requires you to stand in the road while you do it.

If nobody is hurt, you are generally allowed to move the vehicles. Use that. If the other party's body language reads wrong, stay belted in with the doors locked, photograph through the glass, and drive to the nearest police station or a busy, well-lit forecourt to swap details there. A dual-channel dash cam with parking mode costs less than one panel respray and is the only witness that never changes its story. The pattern is depressingly consistent across jurisdictions, whether it is a drive-through queue dispute that ends with a fatal shooting , an Indianapolis confrontation that escalates in seconds , or a parking-lot argument that only ends well because of a steel-toed boot . The trigger is almost never the crash. It is the conversation afterwards.

There is an insurance wrinkle worth knowing too. The Road Accident Fund exists to compensate loss arising from the driving of a motor vehicle. A deliberate shooting that happens after a collision is a criminal act, not driving, so it generally falls outside that safety net entirely. Families in these cases are usually left with private life cover, whatever a civil claim against the accused might yield, and the cold reality that most defendants have nothing to attach. If you drive for a living or commute through high-risk corridors, that gap is an argument for checking the fine print on your personal accident and life cover rather than assuming the state backstop applies.

An empty slot on the Killarney entry list

Killarney's organisers had him on the entry for the weekend, and Motorsport South Africa's statement described a gap in the sport that will not be filled quickly. Both are true and neither is much comfort. South African national racing is a small, self-funded, tight-knit paddock where the same faces have been showing up with the same trailers for twenty years, and losing a two-time reigning hillclimb winner and a recent touring car champion is not an abstraction there. It is a missing car, a stalled team programme and a set of empty seats at scrutineering.

Motorsport has always asked its people to accept a level of risk that outsiders find irrational, and the sport has spent generations earning the right to make that risk smaller. Wolk had every reason to expect that the dangerous part of his week would begin at a green flag. Racing loses figures to illness and to age often enough, as it did with Lancia rally stalwart Alex Fiorio , and the paddock has learned how to absorb those. This is a different category of loss. He died standing still, on a public road, over a dented panel. Three men are now answering for it.

articles.title: Rams WR Puka Nacua inactive, Aaron Donald active for Giants visit on Monday night
articles.summary: All-Pro receiver Puka Nacua is inactive for the Los Angeles Rams' game against the New York Giants on Monday night due to a hip injury, while Aaron Donald is...
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. (AP) — All-Pro receiver Puka Nacua is inactive for the Los Angeles Rams ' game against the New York Giants on Monday night due to a hip injury, while Aaron Donald is active for the official start of his comeback .

Nacua is missing just the seventh game of his four-year career due to injury when the winless Rams host the unbeaten Giants at SoFi Stadium. He was added to the Rams' injury report on Friday with a hip problem, which is unrelated to the core muscle injury that limited him significantly during training camp and the preseason, according to coach Sean McVay.

Donald participated in team warmups before being declared active for his first NFL game since January 2024. The three-time AP NFL Defensive Player of the Year retired in March 2024 , but returned to the Rams late last month.

Donald didn't travel to Australia for the Rams' embarrassing season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers .

Receiver Jordan Whittington is also inactive for the Rams due to a quadriceps injury. The Rams, who frequently use three-tight-end offensive sets, will face the Giants with only four healthy wide receivers: Davante Adams , Xavier Smith , Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell .

Rams safety Kam Kinchens (hamstring) also is inactive.

The Giants' inactives included cornerback Deonte Banks (calf), who had four tackles in New York's season-opening win over Dallas , and linebacker Micah McFadden .

Running back Najee Harris is active for his Giants debut after being a healthy scratch last week. New York signed the four-time 1,000-yard rusher last month after an injury limited him to three games with the Chargers last season.
